A group of people look up at a castle from a boat on the River Lys, which is almost completely green from duckweed

A swarm of ermine moth caterpillars engineered this surreal scene along the Waal River in the Netherlands, encasing a willow tree in silk. The caterpillars, captured by photographer Theo Bosboom, used the ghostly covering as a path to the tree’s leaves and as protection from birds and other predators until it was time to transform into moths and fly off.
Berries from a Mahonia aquifolium shrub. Focus stack of 19 photos.
